objective: Derive an exact bounded-neighbor-recoloring criterion, its sharp list-size threshold, rigid signatures, and the pentagon reduction for at least three degree-two vertices.

atomic_claims.text: For fixed outside colors, repair in {u,v,w} exists exactly when J is not contained in B(I); for I=s+[0,m-1], B(I)=s+[m+6,13].
Available-list sizes summing to at least nine guarantee repair; a seven-vertex tree with size sum eight is a sharp fixed-boundary failure.
In a vertex-minimal obstruction, deleting two adjacent degree-two vertices forces equal endpoint colors c, with both outside-neighbor color pairs equal to {c+7,c+13}.
A five-cycle with at least three degree-two vertices is excluded from a vertex-minimal obstruction by explicit bounded recoloring.

assumptions: Finite simple triangle-free planar graph of maximum degree at most three, with the stated local degrees.
Outside colors are fixed exactly as specified; the two neighbors of a degree-two vertex are nonadjacent.
Minimal-obstruction consequences are conditional on minimum vertex order.
Generated candidates c01 and c03 are explicit mathematical dependencies, not verification receipts.
risks: A local repair failure does not exclude larger recolorings.
The size-eight tree is not a graph counterexample to the ProblemContract.
The pentagon argument does not cover exactly two degree-two vertices.
No mathematical computation or kernel run is claimed.
